I have farmed cotton in Quzhou for 35 years. I know my 13.1 mu of land like the back of my hand. My family has six people, and with some of them working off-farm, I need a crop that I can manage without too much labor at peak times, but cotton is what this soil is best for, so I stick with it. 

At my age, I do not gamble on strange new seeds. I will plant an improved variety—something like the 99-1 or Guoxinmian types that the county seed station sells. They are not traditional old seeds, and they are not hybrids either; they are reliable improved varieties that give good boll weight and handle the local pests better than the old kinds. I buy about 3 jin of seed per mu.

For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer as a base before sowing and topdress with urea later. Cotton needs plenty of nutrition, especially potassium for boll development, so I aim for about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, and around 15 kg each of phosphate and potash. I learned long ago that skimping on potash gives you empty bolls. I till the land with rotary tillage before planting—it breaks up the soil well after winter and makes a smooth seedbed without turning up too much cold subsoil.

Water is precious, but I have my well. I will irrigate three times this year: once around sowing if April stays dry, once when the plants flower in July, and once at peak boll in August. I never flood cotton; too much water at the wrong time causes boll drop and disease. Three careful irrigations give me the best balance.

Pests are my biggest headache. I will spray pesticides about twelve times through the season—mostly insecticides for bollworm, aphids, and red spider mites, plus one herbicide spray early to control weeds. After 35 years, I do not spray on a calendar blindly; I walk the fields and spray when I see the pests building. That saves me some money and keeps the plants healthier.

If the weather is normal and no big disaster hits, I expect to harvest about 550 kg of seed cotton per mu. That has been a solid, achievable yield for me in good years, and with my experience and the inputs I have planned, I am counting on it.
